operation_tail.detail: The planned-deployment collection covers providers included in Ofcom's information-gathering exercise; other providers may also have deployment plans, so the reported universe is not assumed exhaustive.
Provider deployment plans are bound to their January 2026 status and are not presented as continuously current.
For the planned-deployment request, a VHCN must consist wholly of optical-fibre elements at least to the distribution point serving the location.
Ofcom received planned-deployment data for just over 11 million UK premises; this is a submissions volume, not a unique current-coverage count.
A premise may be targeted by more than one network provider and therefore cannot be deduplicated solely by planned-premise appearance.
Multiple plans for the same premise may have different deployment timescales and certainty levels, which remain separate attributes.
Provider plans extending beyond the requested three-year period are excluded from reported findings to maintain a consistent horizon.
Anticipated coverage is calculated by combining stated plans with existing full-fibre and gigabit-capable coverage as of January 2026.
Ofcom reports two forward-looking scenarios: all submitted plans and High Confidence plans only; they are not merged into one certainty class.
The planned-deployment analysis uses a 32.5 million-property premise base; this total remains specific to that methodology vintage.
Of the planned-deployment premise base, 30.5 million properties are classified as residential.
The methodology classifies 26.1 million residential premises as urban and does not infer urbanity from postcode text.
The methodology classifies 4.3 million residential premises as rural and retains the stated classification source.
Ofcom recalculates the premise base for each Connected Nations update rather than carrying a fixed property universe forward indefinitely.
The AddressBase release closest to the collected-information reference date is selected for each premise-base calculation.
Epoch 123, released in November 2025, is the AddressBase vintage used for the Spring 2026 premise base.
The planned-deployment premise base uses the November 2025 ONS National Statistics Postcode Lookup for additional geography classifications.
Locale assigns each census output area to one of seven groups; the grouping is retained as a third-party classification.
Locale Groups A through E map to Urban for this analysis.
Locale Groups F and G map to Rural for this analysis.
The planned FWA analysis uses deployment data from two mobile network operators and one wireless internet service provider.
FWA operators supplied three-year plans to extend or upgrade network infrastructure from the January 2026 reference date.
A planned FWA mast is in scope when supported by fibre or by other backhaul capable of at least 1 Gbit/s.
Ofcom notes that wireless operators could not guarantee 100 Mbit/s service to a particular property, so mast plans are not property-speed promises.
High-capacity backhaul indicates that a mast could attain a 100 Mbit/s service level if a suitable antenna is installed; it is not proof of delivered service.
The future FWA collection records mast-site identity, location and anticipated deployment timescale rather than parcel coverage rows.
Individual property address matching is not performed for planned FWA deployments.
Future FWA deployment is reported solely through relevant mast locations and cannot be promoted to exact premise availability.
The broadband checker uses Ordnance Survey property data as its base dataset; checker identity is not derived from free-text postcode alone.
Ofcom directs users to the provider for outage status, so a checker coverage result is not treated as live service-health evidence.
The checker defines standard broadband as services delivering download speeds up to 30 Mbit/s.
The checker defines ultrafast broadband as download speeds above 300 Mbit/s.
FWA checker coverage is produced by operator predictive modelling and is not an observed parcel-level measurement.
Checker speed predictions are supplied by leading UK broadband networks and are not assumed to represent every provider.
Some network providers, particularly smaller networks, may not yet be included in Ofcom's checker collection.
The checker displays the fastest estimated speeds predicted by network operators, not an average or guaranteed speed.
Actual service availability at a property may differ from the checker's prediction.
The speed received by a user may differ from the estimated speed shown in the checker.
The performance of the in-building network is recorded as a factor that can reduce received speed.
Multiple devices using online services at the same time can reduce the speed experienced on a device.
The physical length of the line can affect received broadband performance.
The age of the line is a documented factor that may affect broadband performance.
The repair condition of the line can affect performance and may require provider action.
A network provider shown in coverage data may not sell services directly to customers.
Where a network provider is wholesale-only, service purchasing requires identifying resellers rather than treating the infrastructure provider as the retailer.
Ofcom lists network-provider names and web details only when the provider has expressly permitted publication.
An operator may contribute coverage data without its name being displayed, so displayed provider names are not a complete coverage-source list.
There can be a delay between network deployment in an area and service becoming available to consumers.

Fifty official planned-deployment, FWA, checker, speed-factor and Open Government Licence controls were published line by line; exact coverage candidates remain unchanged pending strict r2 bytes.
